An ensemble forecast system runs the same numerical weather model many times with slightly different initial conditions and model physics, producing a spread of possible outcomes instead of a single answer. The perturbations are designed to sample the uncertainty in the initial analysis, which arises from sparse observations and measurement error. As the integration proceeds, small differences grow nonlinearly in unstable flow, so the spread at a given lead time indicates how predictable the situation is. Forecasters examine the ensemble mean, which smooths unpredictable detail, along with probabilities such as the fraction of members exceeding a rainfall threshold. For skill to be useful, the spread must match the actual forecast error; this property, called reliability, is verified against observations and corrected statistically when the system is over- or under-dispersive.
